Stated Claim / Post Context:
Trump’s Christian Allies Rattled After His On-Air Rage Takes Dark Turn

As Trump’s expressions of “hate” shock religious leaders, an observer of right-wing Christianity explains how his alliance with evangelicals is showing strain—and how Democrats can exploit it.

Actual Article Body:
During his now-infamous interview with CBS News, Donald Trump admitted that he hates his foes with so much fury that he wouldn’t even forgive them in order to get into Heaven. “I do hate some of my enemies,” he said, “and I always will.” Trump’s expression of unquenchable rage has caused widespread consternation among leading Christian figures, including his supporters. Writer Rod Dreher lamented that “he hates his enemies more than he fears God.” Pastor Franklin Graham, a longtime Trump backer, indirectly asked whether Trump has repented sufficiently to avoid Hell. Another backer worried that “Trump is not a Christian.” Still another fretted that he might “end up in Hell forever.” We unraveled all this with Holly Berkley Fletcher, who writes well about right-wing Christianity on her Substack. We discuss why evangelicals support Trump, why their turnout dropped in the last election, how Democrats made headway running as liberal Christians, and whether or not Trump truly fears damnation. Listen to this episode here. A transcript is here.

TNR’s Greg Sargent takes a critical look at the day’s political news and the stories leading NewRepublic.com, and speaks to leading journalists and newsmakers.
